pages.title: A Poem in a Book
pages.content:
It is a cold evening. Yusuf and Grandpa are at home. Grandpa has got an old book. He reads a poem from it. “Grandpa, I like this poem. Who writes it?” Yusuf asks. Grandpa smiles. “Yunus Emre. He is a very famous poet. Look! I have got a story for you.” “Great! I love stories!” Yusuf says.

“Yunus lives in Anatolia more than 700 years ago,” Grandpa says. “He writes poems in Turkish. They are very simple. People understand them well. His poems are about love. Love for Allah, love for all people, animals and plants. People read his poems today, too.”

vocabulary.definition: Words in short lines. Sometimes they sound like a song.

pages.title: A Good Teacher
pages.content:
“Does Yunus go to school, Grandpa?” Yusuf asks.

“Yes, he does,” Grandpa says. “Then he goes to a dervish house. A dervish house is like a school. Many students live there with a teacher. Yunus’s teacher is Taptuk Emre. He is a good and kind man. Yunus says, ‘I want to learn from you. And I want to help you.’ Taptuk Emre is happy. Yunus stays at the dervish house. He works there every day.”

vocabulary.definition: A person who learns to be close to Allah with a teacher.

pages.title: Straight Wood
pages.content:
“What is his job, Grandpa?” Yusuf asks.

“There is a mountain near the dervish house,” Grandpa says. “Every day, Yunus goes up the mountain. He finds wood there. The house needs wood for the fire. Yunus carries the wood on his back. It is very hard work. But Yunus only takes straight wood. Some wood is not straight. He never takes it. He looks for the best wood every day. The wood is like his heart. His heart is straight, too.”

vocabulary.definition: The hard part of a tree.

pages.title: Forty Years
pages.content:
Yusuf thinks. “Every day? For how many years?” he asks.

“For forty years!” Grandpa says. “One day, Taptuk Emre asks, ‘Yunus, why do you only bring straight wood? Is there no other wood on the mountain?’ Yunus says, ‘My teacher, this is a house of good people. Only straight wood can come in here.’ Taptuk Emre is very happy. On the mountain, Yunus looks at the trees, the birds and the rivers. He thinks about Allah all the time.”

pages.title: Flowers for the Teacher
pages.content:
“Does Yunus write poems on the mountain?” Yusuf asks.

“Maybe, Yusuf,” Grandpa says. “Now, listen to another story. One day, Taptuk Emre says to his students, ‘Go to the fields. Bring me beautiful flowers.’ The students run to the fields. They take a lot of flowers. Then they run back quickly. But Yunus comes back very late. He has got only one small daisy in his hand. The other students laugh at him.”

vocabulary.definition: Big open places with grass or flowers.
A small white and yellow flower.

pages.title: One Small Flower
pages.content:
Yusuf opens his eyes wide. “Only one flower? Why?” he asks.

“Taptuk Emre asks Yunus the same question,” Grandpa says. “Yunus says, ‘My teacher, all the flowers say the name of Allah. I can’t cut them. In the evening, this daisy says, “This is my last day. Take me, Yunus.” So, I take it.’ Taptuk Emre smiles. He knows Yunus’s heart. It is full of love.”

Yusuf looks at the old book. “Yunus has got a beautiful heart, Grandpa,” he says. “Yes, Yusuf,” Grandpa says. “A heart with love makes our life beautiful.” Then he reads another poem.
